0101.title: CAREER PLANNER WORKING AREA AND RESOURCES

quotes.text: The nature of career planning requires that the Career Planner's office receive special consideration. The Career Planner's office should be located so it is readily accessible to all Marines during normal working hours. The location should offer privacy during an interview. An office where conversation can be readily overheard is not conducive to establishing good rapport with a Marine being interviewed.

At a minimum the Career Planner should be provided with the computer hardware needed to enhance the effectiveness of daily operations and to access the retention system or other available on-line databases. The following assets should be provided by the local command in order to perform daily retention functions; computer with Internet access, digital camera, color printer, digital scanner and fax machine.
The Career Planner must have a dedicated office space located in an area that is readily accessible to all Marines during normal working hours and provides privacy during an interview.

At a minimum, the following assets are required in order to perform daily career planning functions: (1) Hardware/Software. Laptop with internet access, air card, external hard-drive, web camera, color printer, digital scanner, two Common Access Card (CAC) readers and Adobe Acrobat Pro. (2) On-line Databases. Total Force Retention System (TFRS), Marine Corps Total Force System (MCTFS), Optical Digital Imaging (ODI), Marine Corps Training Information Management System (MCTIMS), Basic Orders System (BOS), Automated Message Handling System (AHMS), ReportNet, etc.

regulatory.summary: The Career Planner holds a private, accessible office and the hardware to run TFRS and the other retention databases. Active commands owe a computer with internet, digital camera, color printer, scanner, and fax. Reserve commands owe a laptop with internet and air card, external drive, web camera, color printer, scanner, two CAC readers, and Adobe Acrobat Pro, plus access to TFRS, MCTFS, ODI, MCTIMS, BOS, AMHS, and ReportNet.

howToInspect.callout: Career Planner cannot reach TFRS or MCTFS from the working area

0103.title: CAREER PLANNER PERFORMANCE EVALUATIONS

quotes.text: Performance Evaluation. In order for Career Planners to be evaluated in an equitable manner, the Commanding Officer will treat the Career Planner as a Special Staff Officer. The CO will act as the Reporting Senior (RS) for the Career Planner but may delegate this authority using the below guidelines: 1. Commanding General Level Career Planners. The G-1/Chief of Staff is the lowest level of delegation permitted. 2. Unit Level Career Planners. The Executive Officer is the lowest level of delegation permitted. 3. Other Career Planners. Career Planners working in other billets where the command structure does not fit option one or two above should provide performance evaluations at the highest level possible.

Performance Evaluation. As a Special Staff Officer, the Career Planner will be evaluated by the Commanding Officer/Inspector-Instructor. The CO/I-I shall act as the Reporting Senior (RS) for Career Planners but may delegate this authority using the below guidelines: (a) Commanding General Level Career Planners. The Chief of Staff is the lowest level of delegation permitted. (b) Unit Level Career Planners. The Executive Officer/Assistant Inspector-Instructor is the lowest level of delegation permitted.

regulatory.summary: The Career Planner is a special staff officer. The commander is the Reporting Senior. Delegation stops at the G-1 or Chief of Staff for CG-level Career Planners and at the XO or Assistant I-I for unit Career Planners. A fitness report with the SgtMaj, S-1 officer, or company commander as RS fails the standard.

actions: Pull the Career Planner's most recent fitness report from MMSB or the Marine's copy.

howToInspect.callout: Reporting Senior below the XO, Assistant I-I, G-1, or Chief of Staff

0104.title: WRITTEN DELEGATION TO CONDUCT INTERVIEWS

quotes.text: Delegation to Conduct Interviews. While the unit CO is directly responsible for conducting interviews for all Marines within the command it is not always feasible for the CO to do 100% of the interviews. In this instance, the CO must delegate, in writing, the appropriate level (i.e. HqCo Cmdrs, MSG Co Cmdrs, OIC's, etc.) to conduct the interviews on their behalf.

The CO may designate the executive officer or Company Commander to conduct Commanding Officer interviews. The Commanding Officer must conduct an interview when the Marine is not recommended for reenlistment.

While the Commanding Officer/Inspector-Instructor is directly responsible for conducting interviews for all Marines within the command, it is not always feasible for the CO/I-I to conduct 100% of the interviews. In this instance, the CO/I-I must delegate, in writing, to the appropriate level (Commissioned Officers and Chief Warrant Officers) to conduct the interviews on their behalf. a. Officers delegated authority to conduct interviews may only interview Marines over whom they have cognizance. b. The CO/I-I must conduct the interview when a Marine is not recommended for retention. c. Authority to conduct interviews will be retained at the highest level feasible.

regulatory.summary: Any officer conducting CO interviews on the commander's behalf holds a written delegation. Delegates are commissioned officers or chief warrant officers with cognizance over the Marine. The commander personally interviews any Marine not recommended for reenlistment or retention.

actions: Request the current commander's written delegation naming who conducts CO interviews.
Confirm it is signed by the sitting commander, not inherited from a predecessor.
howToInspect.callout: Interviews conducted by delegates with no letter from the current commander

actions: From IMM or contact records, list who signed CO interviews in the period.
Confirm each signer appears on the letter and interviewed only Marines under their cognizance.
Confirm every not-recommended interview carries the commander's own signature.
howToInspect.callout: SNCO or unlisted officer signing CO interviews, or a not-recommended interview delegated

questionsToAsk: Who conducts CO interviews for you, and where is the letter?
Show me the last Marine you did not recommend and who interviewed them.
verification: Delegation letter signed by the current commander.
Interview signers reconcile to the letter.
Not-recommended interviews signed by the commander.

0105.title: EAS AND RECC INTERVIEW RECOMMENDATIONS AND RE CODES

quotes.text: The Commanding Officer, or those delegated to conduct interviews, will assign the appropriate Reenlistment Eligibility (RE) Code, per appendix D, during the EAS interview for those Marines who will separate at EAS and for those Marines that are not reenlistment eligible. Additionally, the CO, not their delegate, must assign the appropriate code for those Marines who receive anything other than RE-1A. Appendix D provides details on the qualifications of each code.

Amplifying information must be provided for a recommendation of "Recommended With Reservation" or "Not Recommended". Though a recommendation of "Not Recommended" does not disqualify a Marine from reenlistment eligibility, but it is key input. The authority to provide a recommendation of "Recommended With Reservation" or "Not Recommended" may not be delegated.
The CO/I-I must conduct the interview when a Marine is not recommended for retention.

quotes.citation: MCO 1900.16 CH 2, Appendix I (table rows, columns joined)
quotes.text: RE-1A Recommended and eligible No restrictions to reenlistment. Meets all prerequisites, includes those Marines discharged at EAS while pregnant who would otherwise be eligible. RE-4 Not recommended for reenlistment. Page 11 entry required stating reason for assignment. Individual Marine must sign Page 11 entry. This code may be assigned in lieu of any RE-3 code (except RE-3B and RE-3F) if the Marine's performance warrants and the reason can be documented.

regulatory.summary: At the EAS interview the commander or written delegate records a reenlistment recommendation and assigns the RE code from MCO 1900.16 Appendix I. Any code other than RE-1A and any recommendation of Recommended With Reservation or Not Recommended comes from the commander personally. RE-3 and RE-4 codes require a page 11 entry stating the reason, signed by the Marine.

0106.title: NO MISSED COMMANDING OFFICER INTERVIEWS

quotes.text: Required. The Career Planner and Commanding Officer will ensure interviews are conducted as required.

The Career Planner and Commanding Officer will conduct an EAS interview eight to six months before the Marine's EAS. This interview is not required if a Marine has submitted a reenlistment request or has been approved for transfer to the FMCR.

The prescribed occasions for interviews will be completed within the required time frames for each occasion. Interviews conducted after the required time frame for each occasion will be considered 'Missed'.

(2) Careerist Interview. The careerist interview is a two-part interview required to be conducted by both the CP and CO/I-I with all Marines with a Reserve Component Code of K1 – K4, K8, K9, KA, KB, and KF. This interview is to be conducted between 1 July and 31 October immediately prior to the Marine's Reserve End of Current Contract (RECC). (3) RECC Interview. The RECC interview is a two-part interview required to be conducted by both the CP and CO/I-I with all Marines with a Reserve Component Code of K1 – K4, K8, K9, KA, KB, and KF. This interview is to be conducted no earlier than 3 months prior to the month in which the Marine's RECC resides and no later than the Marine's RECC.

If a required interview cannot be conducted prior to becoming 'Missed', the Career Planner will make administrative notes depicting the circumstances in the IMM. These notes will be validated via signature by CP and CO/I-I in the IMM. The required interview will be conducted with the Marine at the earliest possible opportunity utilizing a voluntary interview in the IMM.

regulatory.summary: Active: the CO EAS interview falls eight to six months before EAS unless the Marine has a reenlistment request in or FMCR approval. Reserve: the CO shares the careerist interview (1 July to 31 October before the RECC fiscal year) and the RECC interview (three months before the RECC month through the RECC), plus AR occasions. IMM marks anything outside its window Missed. A missed interview carries a signed administrative note and a follow-up voluntary interview.

0107.title: COMMANDING OFFICER EAS INTERVIEW CONTENT

quotes.text: (b) Review the Marine's plans for separation; re-address the benefits of staying Marine. (c) The primary purpose of the EAS interview is to ensure the Marine is apprised of the benefits of joining the Selected Marine Corps Reserve, Transition Assistance Management Programs and advise him/her on the Marine 4 Life program. Also advise the Marine of the requirement to attend a mandatory pre-separation brief. Both the Commanding Officer and the Career Planner will conduct EAS interviews.

It is the responsibility of Commanding Generals, Commanding Officers, and Officers-In-Charge to ensure all Marines who choose to separate at EAS are briefed on Marine Corps Reserve benefits and obligations.

regulatory.summary: The CO EAS interview covers five points: the Marine's separation plan, the case for staying Marine, Selected Marine Corps Reserve benefits, transition assistance and Marine for Life, and the mandatory pre-separation brief. The record shows each point addressed.

0108.title: COMMANDING OFFICER REVIEWS REENLISTMENT APPROVALS BEFORE EXECUTION

quotes.text: Reenlistment will not be effected, if in the opinion of the commander, the Marine authorized to reenlist has failed to maintain the high standards of professional and personal performance that led to the authority for reenlistment being granted. In such cases the command must immediately inform CMC (MMEA-6) who will then reconsider the Marine's request. Commanding Officers will review all reenlistment packages prior to executing reenlistment.

COs/I-Is shall certify all reenlistment packages by signing the reenlistment authority prior to executing the authority. Reenlistment shall not be executed when, in the opinion of the CO/I-I, the Marine authorized to be reenlisted has failed to maintain the high standards of professionalism, personal performance, and core values after the authority for reenlistment was granted.

regulatory.summary: Between HQMC approval and the oath, the commander reviews the package and certifies the Marine still meets the standard. The Reserve order requires the commander's signature on the reenlistment authority itself. A Marine whose conduct changed after approval is not reenlisted until MMEA or RA reconsiders.

actions: From TFRS, list reenlistments executed in the period.
For each, locate the approved RELM response and the commander's review evidence dated before the DD Form 4 execution date.
howToInspect.callout: Reenlistment executed with no commander review before the oath

actions: Ask how the command stops a reenlistment when misconduct surfaces after approval.
Look for any case where CMC was notified and the approval reconsidered.
howToInspect.callout: No process to hold a reenlistment after approval

questionsToAsk: Show me the commander's signature on an approved RELM before the DD Form 4.

verification: Commander review evidence predates execution on sampled reenlistments.

0109.title: COMMANDING OFFICER SIGNS AND DATES RELM RESPONSES

quotes.text: Forward completed requests for reenlistment or extensions of Regular Marines to CMC (MMEA-6) via the electronic processing system. The Career Planner must ensure that Marines meet the reenlistment prerequisites contained in Chapter 4 of this manual prior to submission of the request. Career Planners will also ensure that Commanding Officers sight and sign all RELM responses from CMC (MMEA-6).
COs/I-Is shall certify all reenlistment packages by signing the reenlistment authority prior to executing the authority.

regulatory.summary: Every RELM response from HQMC, approved or disapproved, is sighted, signed, and dated by the commander. The Career Planner owns getting it in front of the commander. TFRS carries the response page and training guidance on where the signature lands.

0110.title: SENIOR ENLISTED LEADER SCREENS FOR SPECIAL DUTY AND B BILLETS

quotes.text: Screen personnel within the command for assignment to special duty assignments, screen able "B" billets and overseas assignments.
Assist the commander with, retention, career development, retirement, and separations of all Marines in the command.

The unit Commanding Officers have the most important role in the screening process. They are responsible for the initial screening and personal interview of their Marines and final re-certification before detachment.

regulatory.summary: The First Sergeant or Sergeant Major screens Marines for special duty assignments, screenable B billets, and overseas assignments as a stated MOS duty, and assists the commander with retention and career development. The screening product feeds the commander's certification under MCO 1326.6.

0111.title: RE-CERTIFICATION TIMELINES FOR SDA AND B BILLETS

quotes.text: Initially, Commanding Officers are required to certify that the Marines meet the required eligibility criteria during the volunteer submission, or within 60 days of the receipt of orders. No less than 45 days prior to departure, Commanding Officers will re-certify that the selected Marine remains qualified. Commanding Officers may request a deferment, a waiver/exception to policy, or cancellation of orders for Marines who do not meet one or more eligibility requirements.
Commanders Re-certification. No earlier than 60 days and no later than 45 days prior to class report date, Commanding Officers will re-certify that a Marine remains qualified for recruiting duty.

Commanders Re-certification. No earlier than 60 days and no later than 45 days prior to class report date, Commanding Officers will re-certify that a Marine remains qualified for Drill Instructor duty.

Annual Certification. Commanders, (O5 and above) will certify annually (via page 11 or naval correspondence) that all Marines eligible for SDAP remain qualified to serve in the special duty assignment designated for SDAP.

regulatory.summary: Initial certification comes with the volunteer package or within 60 days of orders. Re-certification lands no earlier than 60 and no later than 45 days before the class report or departure date for recruiting, drill instructor, and other Type-1 billets. Marines already in an SDA are re-certified annually for SDAP. The senior enlisted leader tracks the windows so the commander signs on time.

0201.title: CAREER PLANNER ADDITIONAL DUTIES

quotes.text: All Marines routinely perform additional duties, however, commanders should make every effort not to assign additional duties to the Career Planner which will compromise their position, demand a preponderance of their time, or pose a conflict of interest. Those billets include, but are not limited to: Substance Abuse Control Officer (SACO), Legal NCO, Classified Material Systems (CMS) Custodian, Equal Opportunity Representative/Advisor (EOR/EOA), etc.

Restrictions applicable to PMOS 4821 Career Planners. Substance Abuse Control Officer (SACO), Legal NCO, Classified Material Systems (CMS) Custodian, Equal Opportunity Representative/Advisor (EOR/EOA), Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR), Uniformed Victim Advocate (UVA), Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC), Uniformed Readiness Coordinator, Toys for Tots Coordinator, Billet Identification Code Manager (BIC), etc.
Career Planners cannot be designated as UTCs.
Career Planners cannot be designated as UTCs.

regulatory.summary: The Career Planner holds no duty compromising the position, eating most of the day, or creating a conflict. Named exclusions: SACO, Legal NCO, CMS Custodian, EOR or EOA, SAPR roles, UVA, SARC, Uniformed Readiness Coordinator, Toys for Tots, BIC Manager. Unit Transition Coordinator is barred outright by both the MARADMIN and MCO 1700.31A.

0202.title: CAREER PLANNING RECORDS MAINTAINED

quotes.text: Career planning contact records will be maintained in three separate binders. (a) Open Binder. (b) Working Binder. (c) Closed Binder. Contact records will be closed when the Marine detaches, separates or reenlists. (d) Contact Record binders will be maintained for the current FY (including those in the open binder) and 2 previous fiscal years then destroyed per reference (ab) SSIC 1040.2.

0203.title: NO MISSED CAREER PLANNER INTERVIEWS

quotes.text: The Career Planner will conduct an initial interview on ALL First Term Marines between 26 and 24 months prior to the Marine's ECC. FTAP Interview. The Career Planner will conduct an FTAP interview between 14-12 months from the Marine's ECC.

Careerist Interview. The Career Marine's interview will be conducted 14-12 months from current ECC, except for Marines approved for transfer to the FMCR or retirement. EAS Interviews. The Career Planner and Commanding Officer will conduct an EAS interview eight to six months before the Marine's EAS.
Identify Marines to be interviewed via the Interview Management Module (IMM). Emphasis should be placed on "Due" and "Overdue" interviews.

(a) For Marines with a future MDPSD, this interview is to be conducted between 1 July and 31 October immediately prior to the Marine's MDPSD. (b) For Marines without a MDPSD or with a MDPSD that has passed, this interview is to be conducted between 1 July and 31 October immediately prior to the Marine's MSO.

AR Interviews. (1) ARAP Interview. This interview is to be conducted between 1 June and 31 August prior to the fiscal year in which the Marine's ECC resides. (2) AR EAS Interview. This interview is to be conducted no earlier than 6 months prior to the month in which the Marine's EAS resides and no later than 3 months prior to the Marine's EAS.

regulatory.summary: Active windows: initial 26 to 24 months before ECC, FTAP 14 to 12 months, careerist 14 to 12 months, EAS 8 to 6 months, NCS three months before EAS. Reserve windows: first term and careerist 1 July to 31 October before the governing date, RECC three months before the RECC month, ARAP 1 June to 31 August, AR EAS 6 to 3 months. IMM flags Due, Overdue, and Missed. A missed interview outside its window is a discrepancy regardless of later completion.

actions: Have the Career Planner display Missed interviews for the period by type.

0204.title: INTERVIEWS CAPTURE TRUE REASONS FOR RETENTION DECISIONS

The Marine should also be familiarized with the FTAP process.

quotes.text: This interview is designed to advise the career Marine of current options and benefits such as SRBP, special duty assignments, and to determine reenlistment eligibility. The Career Planner will also counsel the Marine concerning enlisted career force controls and separation pay, if applicable. This interview also allows the Career Planner time to get a CG waiver or recover missing fitness reports should the Marine desire further service.

0208.title: INTERVIEWS DOCUMENTED, COMPLETED, AND ARCHIVED IN IMM

quotes.text: Properly document the CP interview within the Interview Management Module (IMM) in the online retention database. This can be achieved by completing the interview electronically within the IMM or uploading a completed Reserve Career Planning Contact Record to the IMM. Signatures of the Marine and Career Planner are required. The preferred method to obtain signatures will be digital, utilizing dual CAC readers. Properly executed, interviews will provide a chronological record of: (a) The Marine's basic qualifications for retention. (b) The CP's evaluation and guidance to the Marine. (c) The Marine's specific reason(s) for retention or transition. (d) The recommended RE-Code (as applicable).

The career planning personnel shall transcribe the CO's recommendation and comments into the IMM within the online retention database. Career planning personnel will reconcile the CO's interview within the IMM.

(1) Results of all interviews that are conducted between the individual Marine, CP, and CO, will be captured and maintained within the IMM. (2) In instances where the use of the IMM is not feasible or practical, the Reserve Career Planning Contact Record is authorized. Interview notes captured on the Reserve Career Planning Contact Record will be transferred into the IMM once available.

regulatory.summary: Every interview closes in IMM with Marine and Career Planner signatures, digital where possible, and the four record elements: qualifications, evaluation and guidance, the Marine's reasons, and the recommended RE code. CO interviews are transcribed and reconciled in IMM. Paper contact records are a bridge, transferred into IMM when available.

0209.title: REQUIRED INTERVIEW TOPICS COVERED

quotes.text: All prescribed interviews shall, at a minimum, educate the individual Marine on the following topics: (1) Retention prerequisites to include enlisted career force controls. (2) The need to have a complete and competitive performance record. (3) Career enhancement opportunities to include Professional Military Education (PME) requirements for grade, career progression courses, and special duty assignments. (4) Incentives for which the Marine is eligible based on current policies and programs. (5) Available career paths: SMCR, IRR, AR, IMA and augmentation to the active component. (6) Benefits of a career in the MCR, to include but not limited to obtaining a reserve retirement and Tricare Reserve Select. (7) Eligibility requirements for Post-9/11 GI Bill, Transfer of Education Benefit (TEB), Montgomery GI Bill (MGIB), Montgomery GI Bill-Selected Reserve (MGIB-SR), Marine Corps Tattoo Policy and MOS eligibility requirements. (8) For Marines entering, or currently in, the IRR: Updating contact information and changes in dependent status via Marine On-line (MOL) and Marine Corps Individual Reserve Support Activity (MCIRSA) points of contact.

regulatory.summary: Eight topics ride every required Reserve interview: prerequisites and ECFC, the competitive record, PME and career enhancement, incentives, career paths across SMCR, IRR, AR, IMA, and augmentation, Reserve career benefits including retirement and Tricare Reserve Select, education benefit eligibility with tattoo and MOS rules, and IRR contact maintenance. First-term, careerist, and RECC occasions each add their own extra topics.

Final - Conduct between six and nine months of the Career Planner joining a unit. (b) Career Planners with more than one year on the Career Planning Force are required to have annual evaluations.

0401.title: COLLATERAL DUTY CAREER PLANNERS ASSIGNED

quotes.text: Collateral Duty Career Planner (CDCP). Commanders/I-Is shall assign Active Reserve (AR) or Active Component (AC) Marines as Collateral Duty Career Planners for units without an assigned PMOS 4821 Career Planner. However, special duty assignment pay and the issuance of the dress blue uniform allowance are not authorized per references (a) and (b). Additionally, CDCPs shall meet the following prerequisites prior to appointment: (1) Be in the grade of E5 through E8. (2) Possess a minimum of 24 months remaining on station at date of appointment. (3) Possess current Secret security clearance eligibility and be verified by the unit security manager. (4) Completion of the MarineNet Career Planner Course.
At a minimum, CPs will be assigned to Battalion, Squadron, and equivalent level commands.
